name: journalctl
title: Query the systemd journal
description: Reads logs collected by systemd-journald. This is the primary way to inspect service logs on modern Linux distributions.

flags.name: -u
flags.description: Show entries for one systemd unit only.

flags.name: -f
flags.description: Follow the journal, printing new entries as they arrive.

flags.name: -n
flags.description: Show only the last N entries.

flags.name: --since
flags.description: Show entries newer than the given time, e.g. '1 hour ago'.

flags.name: -p
flags.description: Filter by priority, e.g. 'err' for errors and worse.

examples.explanation: Shows the last 100 log lines for the nginx service.
Follows all new journal entries live.

risk.sideEffects: Read-only. Some entries are only visible to root or members of the systemd-journal group.

name: dmesg
title: Print kernel ring buffer messages
description: Displays messages from the kernel ring buffer - driver, hardware, and boot diagnostics. Useful when a device, disk, or network interface misbehaves.

flags.name: -H
flags.description: Human-readable output with a pager and relative timestamps.

flags.name: -l
flags.description: Restrict output to the given log levels, e.g. 'err,warn'.

examples.explanation: Shows kernel messages with readable timestamps.

risk.sideEffects: Read-only. Many distributions restrict access to root.

name: Get-WinEvent
title: Read Windows event logs
description: Queries Windows event logs and event tracing channels. It replaces the older Get-EventLog cmdlet and can read modern channels that Get-EventLog cannot.

flags.name: -LogName
flags.description: The event log to read, such as System or Application.

flags.name: -MaxEvents
flags.description: Limit how many of the most recent events to return.

flags.name: -FilterHashtable
flags.description: Server-side filter by level, provider, or time; far faster than filtering in the pipeline.

examples.explanation: Returns the 50 most recent System event log entries.

risk.sideEffects: Read-only. Some logs, such as Security, require administrator rights.

name: docker compose logs
title: View logs from Compose services
description: Shows the combined log output of the services defined in a Compose file, with each line prefixed by its service name.

flags.name: -f
flags.description: Follow log output as new lines are written.

flags.name: --tail
flags.description: Show only the last N lines per service.

flags.name: -t
flags.description: Prefix each line with a timestamp.

examples.explanation: Follows the logs of the api service.
Shows the last 100 lines from every service.
